newsitem.title: USA: POLL - Dlr seen steady vs yen, off peaks vs mark.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Dlr seen steady vs yen, off peaks vs mark.

text.p: The dollar will remain relatively steady against the yen over the next two years, but should shrink back from its multi-year peaks against the mark over the same time period, according to the latest Reuters quarterly economic poll.

Mean and median forecasts from economists at more than 20 major banks in the United States showed the dollar/yen rate, which stood near 114 when the poll was conducted, steady near the 115 threshold until the second quarter of 1998, then edging down near 110.

Dollar/mark, which was trading near 1.76 when the poll was conducted, but popped above 1.80 on Tuesday for the first time since August 1991, was seen peaking and shrinking back below 1.70 over a two-year horizon.

Mean forecasts put the average dollar/mark rate at 1.7498 in the third quarter of 1997 and 1.7432 in the fourth quarter of this year. By the first quarter of 1999, however, the rate was expected to retreat to 1.6833, then fall to 1.6666 by the second quarter of 1999.

"Over the next two quarters the interest-rate cycle is likely to work in favor of the dollar," said Alan Ruskin, chief economist at I.D.E.A. Inc. "But that cycle will eventually begin to move in favor of Germany."
Ruskin, who said he was targeting the 1.84 level in dollar/mark in light of recent action, also said that an expected yen appreciation could weigh the dollar down against the mark as well.

Economists surveyed were calling, on average, for a steady, albeit modest, decline in dollar/yen to the 108.64 level by the second quarter of 1999. The median forecast suggested an exchange rate of 110 yen to the dollar by the same date.
In addition to shifting growth differentials, analysts said the U.S. trade deficit should begin to take its toll on the dollar by early 1998.
The evolution of Europe's planned monetary union over the next year and a half was cited as a key wild-card in forecasts for dollar/mark.
